name: Chicago House
desc: Classic four-on-the-floor 909/808 house with backbeat clap on 2 and 4 and the iconic offbeat open hi-hat. The pumping 'and' open hat is the signature of Chicago house.

name: Deep House
desc: Warm four-on-the-floor with soft rimshot/snare backbeat, gentle ghost snares and a laid-back swung closed/open hat groove. Subtle and rolling rather than aggressive.

name: Tech House
desc: Punchy 909 tech-house with four-on-floor kick, clap on the backbeat and busy rolling sixteenth-note off-grid hats. Tight and groovy with offbeat open hats.

name: French House
desc: Filtered French touch disco-house with solid four-on-floor, clap backbeat and busy offbeat hats plus disco-style ghost percussion. Punchy and bouncy.

name: Acid House
desc: Raw 303-driven acid house with relentless four-on-floor kick, 808 clap on the backbeat and sparse offbeat closed hats with an open hat lift before beat 1.

name: US Garage House
desc: Soulful New York / New Jersey garage house with swung ghost snares dropped on even sixteenths and a gospel-tinged shuffle over a four-on-floor base.

name: Afro House
desc: Four-on-floor house layered with syncopated African percussion accents and tom/conga rolls between the backbeats. Hypnotic and tribal-leaning.

name: Tribal House
desc: Percussion-heavy tribal house with dense conga/tom sixteenth rolls and tom accents driving the groove over a four-on-floor kick and clap.

name: Bassline (Niche)
desc: Sheffield bassline / 4x4 garage: speed-garage four-on-floor with offbeat open hats and snappy backbeat snare driving a wobbly sub-bass. Energetic UK club sound.

name: Ghetto House
desc: Stripped-down Dance Mania Chicago ghetto house: hard 808 four-on-floor, claps on the backbeat and raw offbeat hats. Minimal, raunchy and dancefloor-driving.

name: Detroit Techno
desc: Soulful Detroit techno with driving four-on-floor 909 kick, snappy clap on backbeat and the classic offbeat open hat. Machine-funk with a swing.

name: Berlin Dub Techno
desc: Deep Basic Channel-style dub techno: muffled four-on-floor kick, sparse rimshot backbeat and minimal offbeat hats under cavernous chord stabs. Hypnotic and spacious.

name: Minimal Techno
desc: Reductionist minimal techno with a clinical four-on-floor kick, faint backbeat tick and clicky late-sixteenth hats. Built on space and microscopic detail.

name: Hardgroove Techno
desc: Ben Sims-style hardgroove / tribal techno: relentless four-on-floor with looped percussion, busy offbeat sixteenth hats and rolling conga ghosts. Funky and tools-driven.

name: Industrial Techno
desc: Punishing Berghain-style industrial techno with a pounding eighth-note kick, distorted backbeat and noisy offbeat hats. Dark, relentless and physical.

name: Trance
desc: Uplifting trance with driving four-on-floor kick, clap on the backbeat and the characteristic offbeat open hat alongside a rolling offbeat bassline. Euphoric and propulsive.

name: Hardstyle
desc: Hardstyle built on a distorted four-on-floor kick whose reverse-bass tail fills the offbeats, with a hard backbeat clap and offbeat open hats. The kick is the defining instrument.

name: Gabber
desc: Rotterdam gabber: minimal distorted four-on-floor with a few extra eighth kicks placed strategically and a hard backbeat. Brutal, fast and tight.

name: Electro
desc: 808 electro-funk in the Planet Rock lineage: syncopated tresillo-flavored kick, hard backbeat snare/clap and crisp offbeat hats. Robotic b-boy bounce.

name: EBM
desc: Electronic body music: mechanical pounding eighth-note kick with a rigid backbeat clap and offbeat hats. Martial, metronomic and aggressive.

name: IDM Glitch
desc: Autechre/Aphex-style IDM glitch: displaced kicks, snare on the backbeat surrounded by chopped micro-edited ghost snares and erratic hats. Intricate and broken.

name: Breakbeat / Big Beat
desc: Chemical Brothers-style big beat: chunky funk breakbeat kick on 1 and the 'and' of 2, hard backbeat snare and a ghost snare push. Swaggering and heavy.

name: Nu-Skool Breaks
desc: Late-90s nu-skool breaks with a syncopated broken kick, snappy backbeat, funky ghost snares and tech-edged offbeat hats. Funky and bass-heavy.

name: Jungle (Amen)
desc: Classic chopped Amen jungle: kick on 1 and the 'and' of beat 3, snares on the backbeat with the second snare pushed back half a beat plus ghost snares. Shuffled and frantic.

name: Liquid DnB
desc: Smooth liquid drum & bass: tight two-step kick-snare skeleton with a soft ghost snare and rolling offbeat hats under lush musical pads. Soulful and flowing.

name: Neurofunk DnB
desc: Dark technical neurofunk: precise two-step with metallic ghost snares, dense sixteenth hats and a reese bassline. Mechanical, aggressive and sci-fi.

name: Jump-Up DnB
desc: Bouncy jump-up DnB: simple punchy two-step kick-snare with offbeat open hats driving a wobbly cartoonish bassline. High-energy and rave-ready.

name: Halftime DnB
desc: Halftime drum & bass at full tempo with the big snare landing on beat 3, syncopated kicks and trap-influenced ghost snares. Heavy, spacious and head-nodding.

name: 2-Step Garage
desc: Definitive 2-step UKG: kick on beat 1 and the 'and' of beat 3 skipping beats, snare on the backbeat, ghost snares and shuffled syncopated hats with heavy swing.

name: Speed Garage
desc: Speed garage: four-on-floor kick with offbeat open hats, backbeat snare and skippy ghost snares driving a deep rolling sub-bass. Faster, bass-led house cousin.

name: 4x4 Garage
desc: 4x4 / two-step's straight cousin: solid four-on-floor with skippy swung ghost snares on even sixteenths and offbeat hats. The clubbier side of UK garage.

name: Grime
desc: 140bpm grime: syncopated sparse kick, hard backbeat snare and a war-ready 8-bar swing inherited from 2-step garage. Dark, eski and angular.

name: Dubstep (140)
desc: Classic 140 dubstep halftime feel: kick on 1, the big snare on beat 3, syncopated sub-kick and sparse offbeat hats leaving room for the wobble. Spacious and sub-heavy.

name: Brostep
desc: Aggressive US brostep: hard halftime snare on beat 3 with extra layered snare hits, syncopated kicks and metallic hats supporting screaming mid-bass growls. Maximal and abrasive.

name: Riddim Dubstep
desc: Minimal riddim dubstep: stripped halftime with a single big snare on beat 3 and a syncopated kick, leaving maximum space for the triplet-bouncing bassline. Repetitive and hypnotic.

name: Future Garage
desc: Atmospheric future garage: skippy 2-step kick-snare framework with ghost snares, late off-grid hats and reverb-drenched space. Moody, swung and emotive.

name: Footwork / Juke
desc: 160bpm Chicago footwork/juke: rapid syncopated tresillo-driven 808 kicks, claps and stuttering triplet-feel snares with chopped vocals. Frantic and polyrhythmic.

name: Baltimore Club
desc: Baltimore club: the signature five-beat syncopated kick pattern with breakbeat snares and chopped vocal stabs at ~130bpm. Bouncy, repetitive and party-driving.

name: Jersey Club
desc: Jersey club: two quarter kicks then the signature dotted-eighth triplet kick run, bed-squeak sample and chopped vocals. Bouncy, stuttering and ~140bpm.

name: Philly Club
desc: Philadelphia club: a faster, busier kick variant of the Baltimore lineage with dense syncopated bass drums, chopped vocals and breakbeat snares. Relentless and energetic.

name: Ballroom / Vogue
desc: Ballroom / vogue beat built on a four-on-floor kick, clap on the backbeat and the iconic crash/chant on the '5-count' for dip and spin. Dramatic and runway-ready.

name: Atlanta Trap
desc: Atlanta trap: booming syncopated 808 glides, snare/clap on the backbeat and fast rolling sixteenth hats with triplet rolls. The signature ATL bounce.

name: UK Drill
desc: UK drill: sliding syncopated 808 bass on the offbeats, snare on the backbeat and skippy hats inherited from UK garage at ~140bpm. Dark, sparse and menacing.

name: NY Drill
desc: Brooklyn drill: punchy sliding 808s, hard backbeat snare and the signature reversed/skittering hat patterns over a sample-flip. Aggressive and bouncy.

name: Chicago Drill
desc: Original Chicago drill: dark halftime feel with the snare landing on beat 3, sparse booming 808s and triplet hat rolls. Ominous, slow-burning and heavy.

name: Boom Bap
desc: 90s boom bap: punchy kick on 1 with a syncopated push, hard snare on the backbeat, ghost snare and swung eighth hats. Dusty, sample-chopped and head-nodding.

name: Lo-Fi Hip-Hop
desc: Lo-fi hip-hop: a loose swung boom-bap skeleton with a lazy off-grid feel, soft snare backbeat and dusty eighth hats under jazzy chords. Relaxed and nostalgic.

name: Neo-Soul
desc: Neo-soul / Dilla-style drunk groove: a humanized off-grid kick-snare with rich ghost snares and laid-back hats. Wonky, soulful and deeply pocketed.

name: G-Funk
desc: West Coast G-funk: a relaxed boom-bap kick-snare with swung hats and offbeat open hats under whining synth leads. Smooth, funky and cruising at ~90bpm.

name: Miami Bass
desc: Miami bass / booty bass: syncopated 808 sub kicks in the electro lineage, hard claps on the backbeat and crisp offbeat hats. Fast, sub-heavy and party-driven.

name: Reggaeton (Dembow)
desc: Reggaeton dembow: kick on beat 1 and the 'and' of beat 2, snare on the 'and' of 1 plus the boom-ch-boom-chick backbeat. The lopsided bouncing Latin groove.

name: Dembow (Dominican)
desc: Dominican dembow: a faster, busier descendant of the Jamaican riddim with extra syncopated kicks and the relentless boom-ch-boom-chick snare. Raw and frenetic.

name: Moombahton
desc: Moombahton: house energy slowed to ~108bpm over a dembow kick-snare skeleton with offbeat open hats. The Dave Nada fusion of dembow and electro-house.

name: Baile Funk (Tamborzão)
desc: Rio funk carioca tamborzão: a syncopated surdo-phrased 808 kick pattern with tight claps on the backbeat and tamborim accents at ~130bpm. Sparse, punchy and loop-driven.

name: Kuduro
desc: Angolan kuduro: hyperactive syncopated kicks driven by percussion and chant, with hard claps on the backbeat at ~140bpm. Frenzied, militant and dance-battle-ready.

name: Afrobeats
desc: Modern Afrobeats / Afropop: a syncopated tresillo-flavored kick, rim/clap accents and log-drum-style percussion with the signature snare on the 'and' of 3. Bouncy and warm.

name: Amapiano
desc: South African amapiano: a deep four-on-floor with shaker-driven offbeat hats and the signature percussive log-drum bassline answering on the offbeats at ~112bpm. Smooth and rolling.

name: Gqom
desc: Durban gqom: dark broken syncopated kicks with no four-on-floor, sparse claps and heavy bass building rolling tension. Minimal, hypnotic and ominous.

name: Kompa / Zouk
desc: Haitian kompa / zouk digital: a rolling syncopated kick with the characteristic snare/rim on the backbeat and a swaying Caribbean groove. Sensual and mid-tempo.

name: Dancehall (Sleng Teng)
desc: The foundational Sleng Teng riddim from a Casio MT-40 preset: a half-time kick on 1 and 3, snare on the backbeat and steady offbeat hats. The birth of digital dancehall.

name: Dancehall (Bam Bam)
desc: The classic Sly & Robbie Bam Bam riddim: a one-drop-influenced kick with snare on the backbeat and a syncopated rim accent. Rootsy, rolling and endlessly versioned.

name: Dancehall (Diwali)
desc: Steven 'Lenky' Marsden's Diwali riddim: a sparse kick under the instantly recognizable syncopated hand-clap pattern that dominated 2002 pop. Hypnotic and clap-led.

name: Dancehall (Drum Song)
desc: The classic Drum Song riddim: a militant tom/kick-driven roots dancehall pattern with snare on the backbeat and rolling fill accents. Deep, percussive and foundational.

name: Jungle Terror
desc: Jungle terror: a moombahton-tempo'd hybrid with tribal syncopated kicks, hard claps and ethnic percussion stabs. Raw, percussive and festival-aggressive.
